Hi Vanessa —

Thanks again for the intro and for giving AnnotaPro a look. Attached is a first-draft SOW (SOW_AnnotaPro_v1.pdf) and a pricing spreadsheet that outlines per-instance evaluation and per-shot labeling rates. Key highlights:

- 10k prompt-eval judgments (mix of binary quality flags + free-text rationale) delivered over 6 weeks
- Sample acceptance tests and inter-annotator agreement (IAA) threshold at 0.78
- Secure upload via SFTP or AWS S3 with optional encryption-at-rest; on-prem option available for sensitive PHI use cases

Thanks Anna — received and reviewed quickly. A few clarifying items before we book the ops call:

- Can you confirm whether the pricing assumes 1) single-pass labeling (one annotator + adjudication sample) or 2) double-pass with adjudication as default? The spreadsheet has both columns but not the default choice.
- For Acme (PHI-sensitive), we need explicit redaction support and the ability to provide a de-identified subset for external vendors. Does AnnotaPro run redaction pre-processing or do you expect us to sanitize?
- Acceptance tests: can you share the test vector format you use for IAA and whether you provide per-annotator metrics over time?
- Ops question: preferred data ingestion method (SFTP, presigned S3 URLs) and whether you support incremental uploads/resumable transfer for large prompt sets.

I’m attaching a small sample of the prompt slices we plan to use (redwood_prompt_slice_v3.jsonl) — please treat as internal.

If we can get confirmation on the above and a tentative timeline, I’ll loop Lauren (legal) and Marissa (procurement) and set a standing 30-minute slot for Thursday afternoon.

Thanks,

Adding a couple of technical constraints from the SE side:

- We will need token-level annotation support for a subset (~1k examples) to capture hallucination spans. Can AnnotaPro capture start/end token indices and store them in a JSONL column?
- For the remainder (bulk human-quality judgments), binary + short rationale is fine. The rationale should be limited to 2–3 sentences to keep moderation costs reasonable.
- We expect to stream small batches (500–1k items) for sanity checks; prefer presigned S3 URLs with lifecycle rules rather than SFTP if possible.
- Security: we will only consider vendor-managed environments that are SOC2 Type II-certified for PHI-involving work. If you don’t have SOC2, do you provide a description of controls and an opportunity for an onsite audit?

Thanks — I can join the ops call if helpful.

-rishi

Thanks everyone — great questions. Quick updates and next steps: 

- Pricing default: our standard is double-pass with adjudication for quality-critical pilots. We included single-pass pricing as an option; default is double-pass.
- Redaction: AnnotaPro can run a vendor-side redaction pass or accept de-identified payloads. For PHI workloads we recommend client-side de-id + our redaction for residuals; we will sign an addendum to confirm processes.
- Token-level annotations: supported. We deliver start/end token indices in a JSONL column and a CSV summary for analytics.
- Ingestion: presigned S3 URLs are preferred; resumable multipart uploads supported for large batches.
- SOC2: AnnotaPro is SOC2 Type II-certified — attaching certificate and a signed draft SOW (SOW_AnnotaPro_signed_draft.pdf).

Attachments: SOW_AnnotaPro_signed_draft.pdf
Link: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC123-ANNOTAPRO (DocuSign envelope for SOW + DPA)

Timeline proposal:
- Week 0: DPA + PO execution
- Week 1: Ops kickoff, send first 1k test vectors
- Weeks 2–7: Labeling window and iterative acceptance tests

Vanessa — if this looks good, please confirm PO cadence and we’ll send a DocuSign packet for the DPA + SOW.

Best,
